title: Fix weighting potential: wrong generator and edges in coarse-stitch workflow
description:
The weight_stitched.npz shows -7500V at z=1500 (z=150mm). Physics requires the weighting potential to decay exponentially to 0V at the cathode (z=150mm), with 1V at the pixel of interest and 0V at all other pixels.

Root causes identified in test/test-full-3d-pixel-coarse-stitch.sh:

1. Bug 1 (PRIMARY): weight_coarse uses --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid (the DRIFT generator), which applies CathodePotential=-7500V at z_max and sets all pixels to GridPotential=-1000V. The weighting potential coarse domain must instead have: pixel of interest=1V, all other pixels=0V, cathode=0V, but no such full-domain weighting generator exists.

2. Bug 2 (SECONDARY): weight_coarse FDM uses --edges per,per,per (periodic in z). With Dirichlet BCs at both z_min (pixel plane) and z_max (cathode), the correct edge mode is per,per,fix.

3. Bug 3 (MISSING): There is no generator for the coarse full-domain weighting solve. Need to create gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid_full.py that sets pixel-plane BCs (pixel of interest=1V, others=0V) AND cathode BC at z_max=0V, plus a linear-decay initial condition from 1V→0V.
close_reason: Implemented: new pcb_pixel_with_grid_full generator with correct BCs (1V/0V/0V), fixed --edges per,per,fix in test script

title: Fix missing res[:]=0 reset in stencil_poisson_harmonic

title: Make drift PotentialField.efield mask-aware (ghost/mirror) at FR4 surface
description: ROOT CAUSE confirmed: the FDM solve correctly implements no-flux Neumann via mirror/ghost (stencil_poisson_neumann drops bonds to solid cells; verified free cell == mean(active nbrs) to 3e-13, E_perp=0 at face, tangential dphi/dx=8.36 nonzero). But drift_numpy.PotentialField.efield does a NAIVE central difference that reaches into the discarded frozen FR4 cell (phi=0), fabricating a spurious normal Ez spike above the surface and reading (0,0,0) inside the frozen region -> gap electrons get shoved through the FR4 and stop at 9.85 with zero field. FIX: apply the same ghost/mirror rule in efield -- when a +/- sample would land in a solid/insulator cell, reflect it (one-sided gradient) so E_perp=0 and tangential Ex/Ey survive at the FR4 surface. title: near-far-solve: configurable Schwarz overlap (>1 cell) for C1 interface (continuous grad V and grad W)
description: WHY: the induced current i(t)=q*v.gradW uses BOTH the drift velocity (grad V_drift) and the weighting gradient (grad W). Any C1 (gradient) discontinuity in EITHER field at the near/far hybrid interface produces a spurious current glitch each time a drift electron crosses the interface (every electron crosses it). So both hybrid fields need a gradient-continuous interface, not just value-continuous. CURRENT STATE: near-far-solve shares a HARDCODED 1-coarse-cell overlap (pochoir/__main__.py near-far-solve docstring ~line 2281; coupling in fdm_neafar). That converges at only ~0.95/sweep (needs ~100 sweeps) and leaves a ~3%% gradient step (drift: near E_z 48.3 vs far 49.8 V/mm at z=20mm). WHY NOT full-depth fine: memory OK for drift (82M cells ~5.5GB at 50cm) but weighting is 134GB (impossible); and convergence TIME to 2e-11 is ~44h at 50cm (low-freq modes) even for drift. So hybrid is mandatory and the interface must be fixed in-place. FIX: add a configurable overlap (--overlap N, N coarse cells) to near-far-solve; widen the Schwarz overlap region where near(fine) and far(coarse) both solve and blend. Wider overlap (i) accelerates Schwarz convergence (rate improves strongly with overlap width) and (ii) yields a C1 interface. Keep the fine ROI bounded (memory): fine near stays the multi-pixel lateral extent x z=pixel_plane..~30mm; only the overlap depth grows. ACCEPTANCE: (a) v_z continuous across the interface, matching a full-depth ground-truth solve to <0.1%%; (b) grad W continuous -> no induced-current glitch as an electron crosses the interface; (c) converges in a few sweeps (not ~100). Production change: pochoir/fdm_neafar.py Schwarz coupling + __main__ near-far-solve CLI. User-proposed design.

title: Collection model: edge/gap electrons deposit off-conductor (W<1) -> under-collected charge
description: Full-collector charge spans 0.70..0.99966 (mean 0.98); 64/100 wide-gap electrons stop on the FR4 surface (endtag=2) at W~0.01 and are effectively not collected. W transitions 1->0.45 over ~0.4mm at the pad edge, so edge-landers get W(end)<1. Decide the physical model: (a) let electrons slide tangentially along the FR4 surface to the nearest pad before terminating, or (b) snap surface-terminated electrons to the nearest conductor for the Ramo integral, or (c) accept gap-surface charge as genuinely uncollected and report collection efficiency. NOT a 0.05/0.1mm coarsening artifact.
notes: CONCRETE EVIDENCE (task9 charge map): all 100 drift electrons end endtag=2 (FR4 SURFACE) at z=10.0000mm -- the FR4 top face, one 0.05mm cell BELOW the copper pad (z=10.0-10.035mm). NONE reach the conductor (endtag=1). Consequence for the induced-charge map: electrons over the pad INTERIOR stop on the FR4 surface where W~1 -> Q~1; electrons at the pad EDGE stop in the ~0.1mm rim where the W=1 footprint (x=9.5-12.40mm at z=10) is inset from the geometric pad edge (12.5mm) + 1mm chamfer -> W<1 -> Q~0.95 (corner ~0.66). title: Drift field: eliminate v_z discontinuity at near/far interface (z=20mm)
description: Task9/8 drift field uses stitch-near (near 0.05mm + coarse 0.4mm) but SKIPS the overlapping-Schwarz near-far-solve for the drift field (it is run only for weighting). FIRST re-run: developer Step 4b ran but --tol '1*V' > first-sweep near delta (0.608V) => Schwarz stopped after 1 sweep, gradient NOT reconciled: near E_z stayed 48.3 vs far 49.8, v_z step persisted (1.26e-5 -> 1.20e-5, unchanged). Coarse full-domain field is uniform 49.82 from z=14mm up (the true bulk); the fine insulator-aware near sits at 48.3 flat. Tightened --tol '1*V' -> '0.001*V' (matches weighting), --max-iters 6 -> 12; re-running. If multi-sweep Schwarz still leaves a step, it is the near(fine+insulator-mask) vs far(coarse+maskless) mismatch -> developer design (extend fine domain or insulator-aware far).
SECOND re-run (tol 0.001V, max-iters 12): Schwarz now iterates but converges GEOMETRICALLY at ratio ~0.952/sweep (near delta 0.608 -> 0.579 -> 0.552 -> 0.525 ...). Reaching tol 0.001V would need ~100 sweeps (~4h at 2.3min/sweep). 12 sweeps closes only ~1/3 of the 48.3->49.82 gap. Root: minimal (single-coarse-cell) overlap => slow classic Schwarz. The fixed point IS smooth (D-D coupling matches gradient at convergence), so this is a convergence-RATE problem. Practical fixes (developer/design, not a runner tol): (a) increase Schwarz overlap depth; (b) full-depth fine insulator solve (88x88x1201@0.05, ~127M cells, no interface -> no step); (c) determine if far/coarse should be insulator-aware (near=48.3 insulator vs far=49.82 maskless -- near is the more physical field).
RESOLUTION: full-depth fine DRIFT solve (no interface) instead of hybrid Schwarz. GPU mem (float64, ~9 peak arrays, 24GB): drift full-depth fine FITS at 5cm (0.65GB) AND 50cm (5.5GB) because drift is a single-pixel periodic 88x88 tile. Weighting full-depth fine does NOT fit at 50cm (134GB, 440x440 multi-pixel) -> weighting stays hybrid with fine near z<=30mm (7.9GB). Pipeline: coarse -> refine to full-depth fine seed -> fdm full-depth fine (insulator-aware, real cathode BC, no z=20 pin, no stitch) -> velo/drift. Running now (bl5gymz22, GPU1). Weighting interface step is benign (W~0.04 at z=20, W not differentiated for velocity).

The fix stays within the HYBRID solver via the larger-overlap Schwarz (pochoir-2t9m, developer). FIXED via --overlap 15 (pochoir-2t9m). This is exactly the known failure mode (memory weighting-field-must-stay-005mm: coarsening the weighting field 0.05->0.1mm before the Ramo calc causes current spikes/errors). Ruled OUT the two candidate causes in the ticket: (a) phi_w at the electron START points = 0.0003 (negligible, not ~0.02) so 'nonzero weighting at start' is not it; (b) cathode IS grounded (weight3d range is a clean 0..1). Endpoints: all 625 land at z=10.00mm (pad plane / FR4 top); 22/625 on the target pad (phi_w~1), 600/625 elsewhere (phi_w<0.5) -- consistent Ramo. The ~2% deficit for target-pad electrons (phi_w(end)-phi_w(start)=1.0-0.0003=0.9997 analytically) vs the measured ~0.98 is integration error from the 0.1mm weighting field. FIX: run induce on the 0.05mm weighting field (weight_near), not the 0.1mm weight3d -- i.e. do NOT coarsen the weighting before Ramo (aligns with W2 pochoir-tkbm AC2 'weighting stays 0.05mm near pad').

SYMPTOM (1) 'velocity discontinuity at near/far interface' -- NOT reproduced at the seam. velocity/drift3d (0.05mm, 1201 z-cells) is CONTINUOUS across the near far-face z=20mm (cell 400): v_z step at seam 1.26e-5 == neighbouring bulk step 1.24e-5; transverse |dvx| at seam ~9e-11 (numerical noise). title: EPIC: Insulating-surface boundary (Neumann no-flux FR4, NO epsilon)
description:
Implement the insulating-surface boundary condition for the FR4 laminate in the
drift-field solver, on branch `insulating-surface-boundary` (forked from
`wogrid_nearfar` @ a4fedff, the epsilon-deactivated plain-Laplace state).

HARD CONSTRAINT (user): NO epsilon / NO material permittivity of FR4 or any other
material may enter the solver. The dielectric/displacement path (stencil_poisson_
harmonic) stays OFF. This feature is a pure Neumann (no-flux) boundary on top of
plain Laplace on E.

PHYSICAL MODEL
A charged-up insulator reaches steady state when accumulated surface charge cancels
the NORMAL field: E_normal = 0 on the FR4 surface (Neumann). Field lines run
tangential to the FR4 and can only terminate on the copper pads, so gap electrons
funnel to pad edges instead of diving through. Confirmed motivation: with epsilon
active, gap paths dipped ~0.43mm INTO the FR4 (worse overshoot); epsilon is the
wrong lever.

KEY DESIGN DECISION (user-approved)
Model the ENTIRE continuous FR4 slab as an excluded "reflecting" region (no-flux on
all faces), not just its top surface. Simpler and stronger; automatically gives
E_normal=0 everywhere the FR4 is exposed and fully decouples the drift volume from
anything behind the anode.

CELL TAXONOMY (2 -> 3 types)
  - Free (LAr): relaxes to neighbour average (unchanged).
  - Dirichlet (Cu pad, cathode): barr=1, held at fixed potential (unchanged).
  - Insulator (FR4) [NEW]: excluded from the solve; bonds from free cells INTO it
    are cut (no-flux). Marked by a new mask = the continuous FR4 slab the generator
    already builds (cells 168-199 @0.05mm, full transverse extent). Reuse that
    geometry; tag as insulator instead of eps=FR4.

FDM REALIZATION
A free cell adjacent to k insulator cells sums only its (6-k) non-insulator
neighbours and divides by (6-k) (mirror/ghost cell => zero normal derivative).
Precompute a per-cell active-neighbour-count coefficient array + masked neighbour
sum. All tensor ops, torch.compile-safe (no data-dependent branching).

PHASES (see linked issues, chained P1->P5, P6 optional/future)
  P1 Solver core: masked no-flux stencil in fdm_generic.py.
  P2 Solver integration: wire mask through fdm_torch.solve + _compiled_step.
  P3 Generator + pipeline plumbing: build/store/load/pass the mask (--insulator).
  P4 Drift/velo consistency: stop paths at the FR4 surface (surface charge, NOT a
     pad collection).
  P5 Run + physical validation (Task7a): overshoot check => 0 paths below pad.
  P6 (future/optional) Weighting-field consistency for induced current.

CROSS-CUTTING
  - NON-NEGOTIABLE REGRESSION: with no insulator mask, output must be byte-identical
    to today's plain Laplace, at every phase.
  - One phase per session/commit (CLAUDE.md discipline).
  - Concurrency: P1-P2 touch fdm_generic.py / fdm_torch.py (developer active in
    fdm_generic.py) -- coordinate before editing.
  - Deferring numpy/cupy/cumba backends (Task7a uses torch); note explicitly so
    coverage isn't silently dropped.

title: Debug task7a: fdm --epsilon exits 0 without saving potential (leftover sys.exit in stencil_poisson_harmonic)
description:
CONTEXT
Blocks/relates to pochoir-wwo5 (Task7a: activate FR4 dielectric). The Task7a
driver test/run-task7a-dynamic-2cm-fr4.sh (NEPS=1 -> passes --epsilon to the
fdm step in test/run-near2cm-drift.sh) fails: the drift solve produces no
potential, so the run cannot proceed to velo/starts/drift and the `want` guard
would report a missing output (potential/drift_near2cm).

SYMPTOM (reproducible, deterministic)
Running the drift fdm step WITH --epsilon:
  cd test; export PATH="$(cd .. && pwd)/env/bin:$PATH"
  export POCHOIR_STORE=store_task7a_dynamic_2cm_fr4
  pochoir fdm --nepochs 10 --epoch 130000000 --precision 0.00000000002 \
    --edges per,per,fix --engine torch \
    --initial initial/near2cm --boundary boundary/near2cm \
    --epsilon initial/near2cm_epsilon \
    --potential potential/drift_near2cm --increment increment/near2cm
Output:
  ====== epoch: 1/10 x 130000000 ===============
  stencil_poisson_harmonic: max denom = 22.5, min denom = 4.5
  <process exits 0>
No potential/ is written. Exit code 0 (no traceback). A torch Dynamo warning
about the builtin `sys.exit` also appears. Tasks 1-6 (no --epsilon) save
potential normally, because they never enter the harmonic stencil.

ROOT CAUSE (already localized)
pochoir/fdm_generic.py, function stencil_poisson_harmonic:
  line 191: print(f'stencil_poisson_harmonic: max denom = {denom.max()}, min denom = {denom.min()}')
  line 192: sys.exit()
This is a leftover debug print + hard sys.exit() that terminates the process on
the FIRST harmonic-stencil evaluation, before __main__.py fdm reaches
ctx.obj.put(potential, ...) (line ~403). The harmonic stencil is only invoked
when epsilon is supplied, so the bug is masked for the pure-Laplace tasks.
(Note also fdm_torch.py:140 and :149 have commented-out sys.exit() lines —
confirm they are not needed.)

DEBUGGER TASKS
1. Confirm the root cause above by inspection and by re-running the repro.
2. Remove (or guard behind a debug flag) the debug print and sys.exit() at
   fdm_generic.py:191-192 so stencil_poisson_harmonic returns its result
   normally. Keep the change minimal; do not alter the harmonic-mean math.
3. Verify `import sys` usage elsewhere in the file is unaffected; ensure no other
   stray sys.exit()/debug guards remain in the epsilon/harmonic path.
4. Re-run the repro fdm command and confirm potential/drift_near2cm.npz is
   written, is finite (no NaN/Inf), converges, and looks physical (cathode
   -1000V at top plane, ~ -50 V/mm bulk).

TESTER TASKS
1. Reproduce the failing symptom BEFORE the fix (record exit code + absence of
   potential/drift_near2cm.npz).
2. After the debugger fix, run the FULL Task7a end-to-end:
     cd test && ./run-task7a-dynamic-2cm-fr4.sh
   Confirm it completes through paths/near2cm and the overshoot check, output
   in store_task7a_dynamic_2cm_fr4/.
3. Regression: confirm a no-epsilon task still runs unchanged (e.g. Task6
   ./run-task6-dynamic-2cm.sh or Task3) — the fdm path without --epsilon must be
   byte-for-byte unaffected.
4. Sanity-compare Task7a drift paths / pad-plane overshoot vs Task6 (same
   geometry, eps=LAr only) to show the FR4 dielectric effect.

DO NOT COMMIT until the user reviews. Report exit codes, the exact diff, and
before/after evidence.

title: Task7a: activate FR4 dielectric below pixel pad (no shield grid), 2cm drift + 0.7mm chamfer
description:
GOAL
Run the 2 cm drift calculation with 0.7 mm dynamic chamfer (i.e. Task6) but with
the FR4 dielectric of the pixel-plane laminate ACTIVATED. Shield grid stays
DISABLED (GridHoleShape:"None"). Within the 0.1 mm pixel-plane layer: top ~0.05mm
= PCB pad conductor (as today), bottom ~0.05mm = FR4 insulator (eps=FR4Permittivity).
LAr (eps=LArPermittivity) everywhere else (drift gap above pad and below FR4).

INVESTIGATION RESULT (why code is needed)
- Solver already supports spatially-varying permittivity: fdm_generic.py
  stencil_poisson_harmonic(phi, eps) (harmonic-mean face permittivities).
- Plumbing already exists: __main__.py gen stores generator epsilon as
  <initial>_epsilon (taxon permittivity, line ~236); fdm --epsilon loads it and
  passes epsilon=eps to solve() (line ~402).
- MISSING for this case:
  1. gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py builds epsilon ONLY when
     gridHoleShape in ['circular','square'] (line ~485) -> None when grid disabled.
  2. The FR4 fill line is commented out (line ~488); only LAr is ever assigned.
  3. Existing epsilon layout puts FR4/PCB ABOVE the pad (grid-in-drift layout),
     NOT the pixel-plane laminate (FR4 below the pad) we want.
  4. Driver run-near2cm-drift.sh fdm step does NOT pass --epsilon.
  5. epsilon is initialised to zeros and only partially filled -> free cells with
     eps=0 would break the harmonic-mean solve. Must default-fill LAr everywhere.

PLAN
[Code] gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py:generator()
  - Add a grid-independent epsilon build, gated on a new cfg flag
    (e.g. "enableFR4": true) AND LArPermittivity/FR4Permittivity present, so
    Task1-6 (no flag) keep epsilon=None and are byte-unchanged.
  - epsilon = numpy.full(dom.shape, LArPermittivity)  (default LAr everywhere).
  - Set FR4 in the BOTTOM cell(s) of the pixel-plane layer across the full
    transverse extent: epsilon[:, :, pp_loweredge : pp_loweredge+pp_width_pad] =
    FR4Permittivity where pp_width_pad splits the pp_width layer (top cell(s) pad,
    bottom cell(s) FR4). Pin the exact index split during implementation and
    verify with the epsilon plot / compute_chamfer_removed report.
  - Ensure the pad conductor boundary (draw_pixel_plane) covers only the TOP of
    the pp_width layer so the FR4 cell remains a FREE cell (not overwritten to
    boundary). Confirm barr vs epsilon consistency.
[Config] test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_padz10_chamf07_fr4.json
  - Copy of ...padz10_chamf07.json (chamfer_r 0.7, GridHoleShape "None",
    LArPermittivity 1.5, FR4Permittivity 4.5) + "enableFR4": true.
[Driver] test/run-near2cm-drift.sh
  - Add optional env NEPS: when set, pass --epsilon initial/near2cm_epsilon to the
    fdm step (and rely on gen having stored it). Default off -> Task1-6 unchanged.
[Script] test/run-task7a-dynamic-2cm-fr4.sh
  - Modeled on run-task6-dynamic-2cm.sh; STORE=store_task7a_dynamic_2cm_fr4,
    CFG=...chamf07_fr4.json, spacing 0.05, NSHAPE=88,88,601, chamfer 0.7,
    export NEPS=1 so epsilon reaches the solver. Include chamfer report +
    overshoot check.

VERIFICATION
- pochoir gen produces initial/near2cm_epsilon; confirm epsilon array has FR4 only
  in the pixel-plane bottom cell and LAr elsewhere (inspect npz + domain_drift
  eps plot).
- fdm run consumes --epsilon (log shows epsilon loaded); solve converges.
- Compare drift paths / overshoot at pad z=10mm vs Task6 (same geom, eps=LAr only)
  to quantify the FR4 effect.
- Confirm Task1-6 scripts still run unchanged (epsilon=None path).

Added config chamf07_fr4.json (enableFR4:true), run-near2cm-drift.sh NEPS env (--epsilon), run-task7a runner. Verified via pochoir gen: FR4 only in pixel-plane bottom cell (z=200, free), LAr elsewhere; non-FR4 configs produce no epsilon (Task1-6 byte-unchanged). Committed 39d5376. Full fdm/drift solve left to experimenter.

title: Fix odd-pixel symmetry: 0.05mm near-field solve + stride-2 coarsen to 0.1mm for stitch
description:
Pixel sizes that are odd multiples of 0.1mm (e.g. 3.9mm) produce asymmetric FDM pixel tiles at 0.1mm spacing, causing field-response integrals that are neither 0 nor 1. The fix is to run the near-field FDM solve at 0.05mm spacing (where p_size=78 is even and the tile is symmetric), then stride-downsample the result by factor 2 back to 0.1mm before stitching. This avoids the 440×440×6200 full-fine domain that caused OOM in stitch-near.

Why this issue exists: at 0.1mm spacing, p_size=39 (odd) for pixelSize=3.9mm, so half=(39+1)//2=20 gives an asymmetric left/right pixel split (20 vs 19 cells). At 0.05mm, p_size=78 (even) and both halves equal 39 cells. After solving, stride-2 downsampling samples on the same symmetry axis, preserving the correct potential values at electrode surfaces.
design:
Three changes, in dependency order:

1. Fix chamfer_r float truncation in gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py line 223: int() -> round(). This is needed at 0.05mm spacing where int(0.7/0.05)=13 instead of correct 14.

2. Add pochoir coarsen command in pochoir/__main__.py (insert before stitch-near). Takes --input (fine potential), --domain (target coarser domain key, already in store), --output. Infers stride from spacing ratio: stride[i] = round(cdom.spacing[i] / fdom.spacing[i]). Applies arr[::sx, ::sy, ::sz], verifies resulting shape matches domain shape, saves output with taxon=potential.

3. Update run-full-3d-pixel.sh:
   PART A (drift):
   - Keep domain/near: 88×88×401 0.05mm (unchanged - FDM solve)
   - Add domain/near_01: 44×44×201 0.1mm (new)
   - Add coarsen step: potential/near -> potential/near_01 using domain/near_01
   - Change domain/fine: back to 44×44×3100 0.1mm (was 88×88×6200)
   - stitch-near uses potential/near_01 and domain/fine
   PART B (weighting):
   - Keep domain/weight_near: 440×440×401 0.05mm (unchanged - FDM solve)
   - Add domain/weight_near_01: 220×220×201 0.1mm (new)
   - Add coarsen step: potential/weight_near -> potential/weight_near_01 using domain/weight_near_01
   - Change domain/weight_full: back to 220×220×3100 0.1mm (was 440×440×6200)
   - stitch-near uses potential/weight_near_01 and domain/weight_full

Interface continuity is preserved: near-bc pins the z=20mm plane of the 0.05mm near solve to the coarse value; stride-2 retains that plane as index 200 of the 0.1mm result.
acceptance_criteria: pochoir coarsen command exists and works. run-full-3d-pixel.sh completes without OOM. Field-response integrals for pixelSize=3.9mm are all close to 0 or 1 (no values in 0.6-0.8 range).

title: velo fails (KeyError 'boundary') on stitch-near drift potential in run-full-3d-pixel.sh PART C
description:
SYMPTOM: Running test/run-full-3d-pixel.sh fails at PART C 'velo' step (drift velocity) with KeyError: 'boundary'.

ROOT CAUSE: velo (pochoir/__main__.py:419-423) reads the boundary array via the potential's own metadata:
    pot, md = ctx.obj.get(potential, True)
    domain = md['domain']
    bc = md['boundary']        # <-- requires a 'boundary' metadata key
    barr = ctx.obj.get(bc)
In the reference workflow the drift potential was produced by 'pochoir fdm', whose output metadata includes boundary=boundary (params at __main__.py:363-364), so md['boundary'] resolves. In the near-field workflow the drift potential potential/drift3d is produced by 'stitch-near', whose output metadata is:
    dict(operation='stitch-near', domain, near, coarse, stitch_axis, command)
— it has NO 'boundary' key, so velo raises KeyError('boundary').

DEEPER GAP: even if stitch-near added a 'boundary' key, PART A never generates a boundary array for the FULL fine domain (domain/fine, 44x44x1500). 'pochoir gen' runs only for domain/coarse and domain/near. So there is currently no full-domain boundary mask for velo to zero the E-field at electrode cells (pixel plane z=0, cathode at top).

REPRODUCTION (minimal, confirmed):
  stitch-near produces a potential whose metadata keys are
    ['coarse','command','domain','near','operation','stitch_axis','taxon'] (no 'boundary');
  velo --potential <that key> -> exit 1, KeyError('boundary').

SUGGESTED FIX OPTIONS (developer's call):
  (1) stitch-near also emits a stitched full-domain boundary array (upsample coarse boundary + overwrite near boundary) and records boundary=<that key> in the potential metadata; OR
  (2) add an explicit --boundary option to velo and pass a generated full-fine-domain boundary in the script; OR
  (3) make velo tolerate a missing boundary (skip electrode E-field zeroing).
Option (1) keeps velo's existing contract and the downstream pipeline unchanged.

Tester: production code not modified. Regression test added (xfail until fixed): test/test_velo_stitch_near_boundary.py. Related: pochoir-76r (PART C validation).
close_reason: Fixed in commit ee70675 and verified by tester. velo now accepts -b/--boundary (precedence over md['boundary']) and tolerates a missing boundary (skips electrode E-field zeroing); run-full-3d-pixel.sh PART A gens boundary/fine and PART C velo passes --boundary boundary/fine. Regression tests pass: test/test_velo_stitch_near_boundary.py (5) + driver wiring test_velo_uses_full_fine_boundary.

title: BUG: weighting potential plateaus (~0.011) in bulk instead of decaying to 0 at cathode
description: potential/weight3d (from test/test-full-3d-pixel-weight-nearfield.sh) does not decay to 0 at z=150mm; it plateaus at ~0.011 through the bulk and so appears 'largest' at the far z. ROOT CAUSE: Ramo's theorem requires every non-collecting electrode (incl. the cathode) held at weighting potential 0, but generator pcb_pixel_with_grid only draws the pixel/grid near z=0 and NEVER grounds a cathode plane. The fdm 'fix' edge (fdm_generic.edge_condition) is zero-gradient NEUMANN (halo copies adjacent interior cell), not Dirichlet, so the far wall is insulating -> the pixel's injected flux has nowhere to terminate and the potential floats to ~the pixel area fraction (81/9801~0.008, observed ~0.011). VERIFIED: boundary/weight_coarse has nTrue=0 at the far z face (z=374); coarse solve plateaus at ~0.0112 at z=374; this propagates through stitch (bulk = coarse). NOT introduced by the near-field workflow -- the full-fine reference (same generator + fix,fix,fix) is affected identically.
design:
FIX: ground a cathode plane (weighting potential 0, boundary True) in pochoir/gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py generator() at z = driftZDepth (already present in example_gen_pixel_with_grid.json = 148.0). Add after the pixel/grid is drawn:

  z_cat = int(round(cfg['driftZDepth']/dom.spacing[2]))
  if 0 <= z_cat < dom.shape[2]:
      draw_plane(barr, z_cat, 1)   # mark whole far plane immutable
      arr[:, :, z_cat] = 0.0       # weighting potential 0 at cathode

WHY z=driftZDepth (148mm) not the absolute far face: matches the drift generator's cathode location (pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid draws CathodePotential at driftZDepth) so drift and weighting share the same physical cathode plane. Index: coarse(0.4mm)->370, full-fine(0.1mm)->1480.

SELF-CONSISTENT WITH NEAR-FIELD WORKFLOW: for the near domain (396x396x201, z=0..20mm) z_cat=1480 > 200, so the `if z_cat < shape[2]` guard SKIPS it -> near gen correctly omits the cathode (its far face is the z=20mm interface, pinned by near-bc). Only the full-depth coarse + full-fine domains get the grounded cathode. Fixing the coarse solve fixes the stitched bulk and the interface value the near solve sees.

SCOPE: this also corrects the existing full-fine reference (test-full-3d-weight3D-pixel.sh / test-full-3d-pixel.sh weighting), which shares the bug. Minimal change: one block in the weighting generator; uses existing draw_plane helper and the existing driftZDepth config key. No fdm/edge change ('fix'=Neumann is fine once the cathode is an explicit Dirichlet boundary).

ALT considered & rejected: stamping the far face in the driver (no generic CLI command does a far-z Dirichlet stamp; less reusable) and changing 'fix'->Dirichlet (would break drift, where 'fix' Neumann + explicit cathode is correct).
acceptance_criteria:
- gen pcb_pixel_with_grid on a full-depth domain marks the z=driftZDepth plane as boundary (barr True) with arr=0; on a <=20mm near domain it does NOT (guarded).
- After re-running the near-field driver: potential/weight_coarse decays monotonically toward 0 approaching z=148mm (no ~0.011 plateau); value at/after cathode ~0.
- potential/weight3d (stitched) decays to ~0 by z=148mm; [:,0,:] no longer rises with z; global max=1 at the collecting pixel, far-field ~0.
- Continuity at z=20mm interface preserved (no jump/kink).
- Full-fine reference solve (if re-run) shows the same correct decay.
close_reason: Fixed: ground a Dirichlet cathode plane (boundary True, arr=0) at z=driftZDepth in gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.generator(), guarded for near domains (z_cat>=shape[2]) and configs without driftZDepth. Verified: full-depth (375) grounds z=370 plane (all boundary, arr=0); near (201) skips (z_cat=1480, no interior plane grounded). Root cause was missing grounded cathode + Neumann 'fix' edge -> floating bulk ~0.011. Commit pending.

title: Fix: far domain z_min barr=True kills velocity at near/far interface
description: The gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far generator marks the z_min face (z=10mm) as Dirichlet (barr=True). The velo command zeros efield at all barr=1 cells, so the z-velocity is zero at z=10mm. CompositeDrift routes z>=10mm to the far domain, and when the particle reaches z=10mm, it stalls (vz=0). It never transitions into the near domain, so paths stop at the interface instead of continuing to z=0 (pixels). Fix: set barr[:,:,0]=False (Neumann/free at z_min), matching the two-pass FDM intent where the far domain freely determines the potential at z=10mm before bc-zstitch-down reads it.

title: Fix drift paths and induced current: stitch far→near drift BC and increase FDM iterations
description:
Two fixes are required to get correct drift paths and non-zero induced charge.

--- Bug 1: Wrong top BC on near drift domain ---

The generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid sets the entire z_max face (z=9.99mm, index 999) of the near drift domain to -7500V (full cathode voltage). This is wrong. The near domain spans z=0→10mm; the physically correct potential at z=10mm is -500V (= -7500V × 10/150mm). The far drift domain has already solved this correctly: potential/drift_far[:,:,0] (its z_min face at z=10mm) is uniformly -500V.

Fix: add a bc-zstitch-down call for the drift field in the run script, immediately after potential/drift_far is computed and before potential/drift_near FDM:

  pochoir bc-zstitch-down       --far-potential  potential/drift_far       --near-initial   initial/drift_near       --near-boundary  boundary/drift_near

This overwrites boundary/drift_near[:,:,-1] = 1 and initial/drift_near[:,:,-1] = -500V, replacing the incorrect -7500V set by the generator.

--- Bug 2: Near drift FDM massively under-converged ---

The Jacobi FDM on a 1D grid of N points needs O(N²) iterations to converge. The near drift domain has N=1000 z-points → ~10^6 iterations needed. The current --epoch 20000 is ~2% of that. After 20k steps, the near potential is nearly 0V for z<9mm (correct value is linear -500V→0V). The FDM log confirms: maxerr=0.095 >> target 2e-05 after 20000 iterations.

With the corrected top BC (-500V instead of -7500V), the gradient is 15× smaller so the domain relaxes faster, but the fundamental O(N²) bottleneck remains.

Fix: increase --epoch for the near drift FDM to 500000 (minimum) or 1000000. The near weighting FDM will need the same treatment once it has the stitched z_max BC from the weighting bc-zstitch-down.

--- Expected outcome after both fixes ---

1. Near drift potential: linear from 0V (pixels at z=0) to -500V (z=9.99mm), with 3D xy modulation near z=0 from pixel geometry (field lines converging into pixels).
2. Near drift velocity: non-zero vx, vy components within ~1mm of pixel plane (funnel effect at pixel edges).
3. Drift paths: straight lines in far domain (correct), then lateral deflection in near domain (z<~2mm) as electrons funnel toward pixel pads.
4. Paths reach z~0mm (pixel plane), not stall at z=10mm.
5. Induced current: non-zero, integrating to ~1 electron charge per path.

--- Changes to test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh ---

In the Drift field FDM section, after 'want potential/drift_far', add:

  pochoir bc-zstitch-down       --far-potential  potential/drift_far       --near-initial   initial/drift_near       --near-boundary  boundary/drift_near

Change --epoch for near drift FDM from 20000 to 500000.
Change --epoch for near weight FDM from 20000 to 500000 (same convergence issue).

--- Verification steps ---

1. After bc-zstitch-down: check initial/drift_near[:,:,-1] == -500V and boundary/drift_near[:,:,-1] == 1 everywhere.
2. After near drift FDM: z-profile mean should be approximately linear: z=0→0V, z=500→-250V, z=999→-500V. xy-std should grow toward z=0 (pixel structure visible in field).
3. After drift: paths should show z reaching <1mm with xy deflection visible at pixel edges. Check arr[i,-1,2] < 1mm for most paths.
4. After induce-pixel: induced_current.sum() should be ~100 * electron_charge (100 paths × 1e charge each).
design: bc-zstitch-down command already exists in __main__.py (line 792). The far drift at z=10mm is confirmed uniform at -500V from a converged far FDM. The near domain shape is (44,44,1000) with spacing (0.1,0.1,0.01)mm. The weighting near domain (396,396,1000) needs the same iteration increase. Consider whether multigrid or SOR could reduce iteration count further in a follow-on issue.
close_reason: Added bc-zstitch-down for drift field in test script (after potential/drift_far, before potential/drift_near FDM) and increased --epoch from 20000 to 500000 for both near drift and near weighting FDM to address O(N^2) Jacobi convergence requirement.

title: Reverse two-pass weighting field order: far-first then near
description:
The current near→bc-zstitch→far order for the weighting field FDM is wrong. The near domain's z_max face (z=9.99mm) is read by bc-zstitch and passed to the far domain as its z_min BC. But the near FDM imposes no Dirichlet at z_max (Neumann ghost cell via 'fix' edge mode), and 20k iterations are far too few to propagate the pixel BC from z=0 to z=9.99mm — the stitched value is ~1e-163 (numerical underflow), making the far domain trivially zero everywhere.

Fix: reverse the order to far-first then near.

Step 1 — Run far weighting FDM first (z=10→150mm):
  - z_max (z=150mm): 0V Dirichlet (cathode) — already set by gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid_far
  - z_min (z=10mm): Neumann (left free, 'fix' edge mode ghost cell)
  - The far domain is homogeneous (no pixel structure), converges quickly
  - Result: a physically smooth weighting potential in the bulk

Step 2 — bc-zstitch far z_min → near z_max:
  - Read far domain z-index 0 (z=10mm face) from the converged far potential
  - Write it into boundary/weight_near at z-index 999 (barr[:,:,-1]=1, values from far)
  - This gives the near domain a physically motivated top BC instead of Neumann

Step 3 — Run near weighting FDM (z=0→10mm):
  - z_min (z=0mm): pixel BCs from generator (pixel of interest=1V, others=0V)
  - z_max (z=9.99mm): Dirichlet from Step 2 stitching
  - Near domain now has correct BCs at both ends; converges to the correct near-field weighting potential

Changes needed:
  1. gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid_far.py: add a new variant or mode that reads the far weighting potential z_min slice and outputs it as near z_max BC (new bc-zstitch direction flag --direction far-to-near)
  2. OR: add a second bc-zstitch call in the run script with swapped --near/--far arguments
  3. test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh: reorder weighting field section — far FDM first, then bc-zstitch(far→near), then near FDM
  4. Verify: after fix, weight_near z=999 should have mean ~0.008V (DC mode from far solution), weight_far z=0 should match weight_near z=999 continuously
close_reason: Added bc-zstitch-down command to __main__.py and reversed weighting field order in test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh: far FDM first → bc-zstitch-down → near FDM. Near domain z_max now gets a physically motivated Dirichlet BC from the converged far solution instead of a near-zero Neumann ghost cell.

title: Debug zero charge and straight-line drift paths in near/far pixel simulation
description: Two critical bugs found after running test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh: (1) induced charge is identically zero, (2) drift paths are straight lines with no lateral deflection near the pixel plane. Root cause analysis performed on test/store outputs. Three distinct failure modes identified: FDM under-convergence, wrong BC at near-domain top, and domain stitching absence for drift field.

title: Debug near/far stitch: frozen drift paths and broken induced current in neafar script
description:
## Problem

The test run in test/store exposes two coupled bugs in test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh:

**Bug 1 – Drift paths are frozen (zero motion)**
paths/drift_near.npz has shape (100, 4200, 3) but every path is stuck at its start (z=148 mm).
Root cause: the script computes velocity/drift_near from potential/drift_near, which only covers the near domain z=0–10 mm (shape 44×44×1000, dz=0.01 mm). The starting points sit at z=148 mm, deep inside the far domain (z=10–150 mm). drift_numpy.py returns zeros for any point outside the interpolated domain (extrapolate returns numpy.zeros_like(pos)), so the IVP solver never moves the particles.

**Bug 2 – Induced current calculation is fed frozen paths**
pochoir induce-pixel consumes paths/drift_near (all frozen), so the resulting current waveforms are meaningless regardless of whether the weighting-field stitching is correct.

## Root cause summary

The near/far separation used for weighting field (bc-zstitch → FDM → two separate potential grids) was correctly implemented. But the analogous operation for the *drift* field was not: there is no stitching step that merges potential/drift_far (z=10–150 mm) and potential/drift_near (z=0–10 mm) into a single domain-spanning potential (or velocity) before running drift paths.

## What needs to be done

1. **Understand existing domain/potential layout**: confirm exact array shapes, origins, spacings, and z-coverage for drift_near and drift_far potentials in test/store.

2. **Design a pot-stitch (or velo-stitch) command**: implement a new pochoir CLI command that concatenates two z-adjacent potential arrays (near + far, with matching x/y shapes and pitch) into one contiguous array + domain metadata, so velocity can be computed over the full z=0–150 mm extent in one call.
   - The stitch point is at z=10 mm (near z_max = far z_min).
   - Must handle different dz (0.01 mm near vs 0.5 mm far) — either upsample the far field or produce a non-uniform grid. Discuss tradeoffs.
   - Alternatively, implement a two-domain velocity interpolator in drift_numpy.py that queries near or far velocity depending on particle z position.

3. **Fix the velocity step in the script**: replace the single 'want velocity/drift_near' with the correct two-domain approach (stitched potential → one velocity call, OR separate near/far velocities with a composite interpolator).

4. **Fix the paths step**: ensure pochoir drift uses the full-domain velocity, starting points at z=148 mm, and a time window long enough to traverse z=148 mm → 0 mm at LAr drift speed (~1.6 mm/us → ~93 us, but 210 us budget is adequate).

5. **Fix or verify the induced-current step**: confirm pochoir induce-pixel with weighting potential/weight_near is correct once paths are real, or determine whether it also needs the stitched weighting potential.

6. **Regression tests**: add or update tests to catch frozen-path and out-of-domain issues.

## Files to inspect
- test/test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh — the shell script with the pipeline
- pochoir/__main__.py — starts (line 576), drift (line 634), bc_zstitch (line 744), velo (line ~480)
- pochoir/drift_numpy.py — VeloField.__call__ (line 65), extrapolate returns zeros (line 62)
- test/store/pochoir_drift_{near,far}.log — confirm FDM converged
- test/store/paths/drift_near.npz — frozen paths evidence

## Acceptance criteria
- pochoir drift paths starting at z=148 mm show monotone decreasing z reaching near 0 mm.
- drift_paths_3d.png shows visible 3D tracks.
- induced current waveforms are non-trivial.
- No existing tests regress.
close_reason: Implemented CompositeDrift in drift_numpy.py and --velocity-far option in 'pochoir drift'; updated neafar script to compute velocity/drift_far and use composite drift for z=0-150mm paths.

title: Phase 7 — Verification and tests for near/far field separation
description:
## Why this issue exists

After the two-pass FDM solves are running (Phases 4–5), we need automated checks that confirm: (a) field continuity at the z=10mm interface, (b) correct BCs at both ends, and (c) physically sensible field values.

## What needs to be done

Create `test/test_near_far_separation.py` with the following assertions. All checks load from the store (HDF5 or NPZ) after running the full script.

---

### Drift field checks

```python
import numpy as np

# Load potentials from store
phi_near = load('potential/drift_near')   # shape (44, 44, 1000)
phi_far  = load('potential/drift_far')    # shape (44, 44, 280)

# 1. Pixel plane (z=0): mean potential over the free (non-pixel) area
#    Pixel pixels should be at 0V; test that the overall z=0 face is near 0
assert np.abs(phi_near[:, :, 0]).mean() < 10.0, 'drift near z=0 face not near 0V'

# 2. Near-field z_max face (z=10mm) should be fixed at -500V
assert np.allclose(phi_near[:, :, -1], -500.0, atol=1.0),     'drift near z=10mm face not -500V'

# 3. Far-field z_min face (z=10mm) should also be -500V
assert np.allclose(phi_far[:, :, 0], -500.0, atol=1.0),     'drift far z=10mm face not -500V'

# 4. Interface continuity: both sides agree
assert np.allclose(phi_near[:, :, -1], phi_far[:, :, 0], atol=2.0),     'drift field discontinuous at z=10mm interface'

# 5. Cathode (z=150mm) at -7500V
assert np.allclose(phi_far[:, :, -1], -7500.0, atol=1.0),     'drift far cathode face not -7500V'

# 6. Far-field uniform drift: E_z ≈ 500 V/cm in interior
dz_far = 0.5e-1  # 0.5mm in cm
Ez_far = -(phi_far[:, :, 2] - phi_far[:, :, 1]) / dz_far  # V/cm
assert np.allclose(Ez_far.mean(), 500.0, atol=20.0),     f'drift far E_z = {Ez_far.mean():.1f} V/cm, expected ~500 V/cm'
```

---

### Weighting field checks

```python
phi_w_near = load('potential/weight_near')  # shape (396, 396, 1000)
phi_w_far  = load('potential/weight_far')   # shape (396, 396, 280)

# 7. Pixel of interest at z=0 should be +1V (within solver precision)
#    Identify pixel center indices from config (pixelSize, pixelGap, Npixels)
assert phi_w_near[cx, cy, 0] > 0.9, 'weighting near: pixel of interest not ~+1V'

# 8. Interface continuity: near z_max ≈ far z_min
assert np.allclose(phi_w_near[:, :, -1], phi_w_far[:, :, 0], atol=1e-3),     'weighting field discontinuous at z=10mm interface'

# 9. Cathode (z=150mm): weighting field ≈ 0V
assert np.abs(phi_w_far[:, :, -1]).max() < 0.01,     'weighting field not vanishing at cathode'

# 10. Field decays monotonically: mean |phi| at z=10mm < mean |phi| at z=1mm
assert phi_w_near[:, :, -1].mean() < phi_w_near[:, :, 100].mean(),     'weighting field not decaying with distance from pixel'
```

---

### Domain metadata checks

```python
# 11. drift_near domain shape and spacing
dom_near = load_domain('domain/drift_near')
assert dom_near.shape == (44, 44, 1000)
assert np.allclose(dom_near.spacing, [0.1, 0.1, 0.01])

# 12. drift_far domain shape and spacing
dom_far = load_domain('domain/drift_far')
assert dom_far.shape == (44, 44, 280)
assert np.allclose(dom_far.spacing, [0.1, 0.1, 0.5])

# 13. weight_near domain shape and spacing
dom_wn = load_domain('domain/weight_near')
assert dom_wn.shape == (396, 396, 1000)
assert np.allclose(dom_wn.spacing, [0.1, 0.1, 0.01])

# 14. weight_far domain shape and spacing
dom_wf = load_domain('domain/weight_far')
assert dom_wf.shape == (396, 396, 280)
assert np.allclose(dom_wf.spacing, [0.1, 0.1, 0.5])
```

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] test_near_far_separation.py exists and runs with `pytest`
- [ ] All 14 assertions pass on a completed store
- [ ] Test clearly reports which assertion failed and the actual vs expected value
- [ ] Tests are skipped (not failed) if the store files do not yet exist (use `pytest.mark.skipif` or equivalent)
close_reason: Implemented: test/test_near_far_separation.py with 14 assertions covering field BCs, interface continuity, E_z uniformity, and domain metadata. All skip when store absent.

title: Phase 6 — Shell script integration for near/far two-pass workflow
description:
## Why this issue exists

Phases 3–5 define the individual steps for near/far field separation. This issue wires them together into the run script so the full simulation executes correctly end-to-end in the right order.

## What needs to be done

Update (or create) the run script — likely `test/test-full-3d-pixel.sh` or a new `test/test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh` — to execute all steps in dependency order.

---

### Full step sequence

```bash
# ── Domains ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Near-field drift domain: 4.4mm × 4.4mm × 10mm at (0.1, 0.1, 0.01)mm
pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_near     --shape=44,44,1000 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.01*mm'

# Far-field drift domain: 4.4mm × 4.4mm × 140mm at (0.1, 0.1, 0.5)mm, origin z=10mm
pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_far     --shape=44,44,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'

# Near-field weighting domain: 39.6mm × 39.6mm × 10mm at (0.1, 0.1, 0.01)mm
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_near     --shape=396,396,1000 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.01*mm'

# Far-field weighting domain: 39.6mm × 39.6mm × 140mm at (0.1, 0.1, 0.5)mm, origin z=10mm
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_far     --shape=396,396,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'

# ── Geometry generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Near-field drift geometry (pixel plane, PCB, FR4, hole)
pochoir gen --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid     --domain domain/drift_near     --initial initial/drift_near --boundary boundary/drift_near     test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json

# Far-field drift geometry (flat faces only: z_min=-500V, z_max=-7500V, linear ramp interior)
pochoir gen --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far     --domain domain/drift_far     --initial initial/drift_far --boundary boundary/drift_far     test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json

# Near-field weighting geometry (pixel of interest=+1V, others=0V)
pochoir gen --generator pcb_pixel_with_grid     --domain domain/weight_near     --initial initial/weight_near --boundary boundary/weight_near     test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json

# Far-field weighting geometry (all zeros, z_max=0V fixed, z_min free for bc-zstitch)
pochoir gen --generator pcb_weight_pixel_with_grid_far     --domain domain/weight_far     --initial initial/weight_far --boundary boundary/weight_far     test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json

# ── Drift field FDM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Far field first (z=10mm→150mm; BC: z_min=-500V, z_max=-7500V)
pochoir fdm --initial initial/drift_far --boundary boundary/drift_far     --potential potential/drift_far --increment increment/drift_far     --edges per,per,fix --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002

# Near field second (z=0→10mm; BC: pixel plane at 0V, z_max=-500V)
pochoir fdm --initial initial/drift_near --boundary boundary/drift_near     --potential potential/drift_near --increment increment/drift_near     --edges per,per,fix --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002

# ── Weighting field FDM ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Near field first (z=0→10mm; BC: pixel of interest=+1V, others=0V)
pochoir fdm --initial initial/weight_near --boundary boundary/weight_near     --potential potential/weight_near --increment increment/weight_near     --edges per,per,fix --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002

# Stitch near-field z=10mm slice into far-field z_min BC
pochoir bc-zstitch     --near-potential potential/weight_near     --far-initial   initial/weight_far     --far-boundary  boundary/weight_far

# Far field second (z=10mm→150mm; BC: z_min from bc-zstitch, z_max=0V)
pochoir fdm --initial initial/weight_far --boundary boundary/weight_far     --potential potential/weight_far --increment increment/weight_far     --edges per,per,fix --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002

# ── Downstream (unchanged from existing workflow) ─────────────────────────

pochoir velo --temperature '89*K'     --potential potential/drift_near     --velocity velocity/drift_near

# ... electron drift, response combination etc. follow existing script
```

---

### Key ordering constraints

1. `gen` steps must precede their corresponding `fdm` steps
2. `fdm drift_far` must precede `fdm drift_near` (conceptual ordering; technically independent since -500V BC is analytic)
3. `fdm weight_near` must precede `bc-zstitch`
4. `bc-zstitch` must precede `fdm weight_far`

---

### want/cache pattern

The script should use the `want` helper (or equivalent Makefile target) so steps are skipped if output already exists, enabling incremental reruns.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Script runs end-to-end without error from a clean store
- [ ] All six FDM solves produce non-empty potential files
- [ ] bc-zstitch step executes between weight_near FDM and weight_far FDM
- [ ] Downstream velocity/drift steps use potential/drift_near (not the old drift3d)
close_reason: Implemented: test/test-full-3d-pixel-neafar.sh with full near/far two-pass sequence using want helper. Also fixed bc-zstitch option names.

title: Phase 5 — Two-pass weighting field FDM (near then far via bc-zstitch)
description:
## Why this issue exists

The weighting field BCs originate at the pixel plane (z=0), so near field is solved first. The solution at z=10mm then becomes the z_min BC for the far-field solve. The bc-zstitch command (implemented in pochoir-qqe) performs this hand-off.

## What needs to be done

Three sequential steps: near-field FDM → bc-zstitch → far-field FDM.

---

### Step 1 — Near-field weighting FDM

Prereqs: domain/weight_near (396×396×1000, dz=0.01mm) and initial/weight_near, boundary/weight_near from Phase 2 generator. The generator marks the pixel of interest at +1V and all other pixel-plane pixels at 0V. z_max face (z=10mm) is initially open (all free, 0V initial value).

```bash
pochoir fdm     --initial initial/weight_near     --boundary boundary/weight_near     --potential potential/weight_near     --increment increment/weight_near     --edges per,per,fix     --engine torch     --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002
```

**Boundary conditions:**
- z_min face (z=0): pixel of interest = +1V; all other pixel pixels = 0V (set by generator)
- z_max face (z=10mm): free (the FDM solution naturally decays toward 0 as distance from pixel grows)
- x, y: periodic

**Expected result:** potential/weight_near decays from ~+1V near the pixel to near 0V by z=10mm. The z=10mm slice potential/weight_near[:,:,-1] encodes the long-range weighting field that seeds the far-field solve.

---

### Step 2 — bc-zstitch: transfer near-field z=10mm slice to far-field BC

```bash
pochoir bc-zstitch     --near-potential potential/weight_near     --far-initial   initial/weight_far     --far-boundary  boundary/weight_far
```

**What bc-zstitch does:**
1. Reads slice: `bc_slice = potential/weight_near[:, :, -1]`  — shape (396, 396), the z=10mm face
2. Writes into far initial: `initial/weight_far[:, :, 0] = bc_slice`
3. Marks as fixed BC: `boundary/weight_far[:, :, 0] = True`
4. Saves updated initial/weight_far and boundary/weight_far back to the store

No interpolation: x,y spacing is 0.1mm in both near and far, so indices align exactly.

**This step must run AFTER Step 1 (potential/weight_near must exist) and BEFORE Step 3 (far-field fdm reads the updated initial/boundary).**

---

### Step 3 — Far-field weighting FDM

Prereqs: domain/weight_far (396×396×280, dz=0.5mm) from Phase 3 generator (initial all zeros, z_max fixed at 0V). After bc-zstitch, z_min face is also fixed with values from Step 1.

```bash
pochoir fdm     --initial initial/weight_far     --boundary boundary/weight_far     --potential potential/weight_far     --increment increment/weight_far     --edges per,per,fix     --engine torch     --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002
```

**Boundary conditions:**
- z_min face (z=10mm): values from potential/weight_near[:,:,-1], fixed (set by bc-zstitch)
- z_max face (z=150mm): 0V fixed (set by Phase 3 generator — weighting field vanishes at cathode)
- x, y: periodic

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] potential/weight_near solved; values decay from ~+1V at z=0 toward 0V by z=10mm
- [ ] bc-zstitch runs without error; boundary/weight_far[:,:,0] is True after stitch; values match potential/weight_near[:,:,-1]
- [ ] potential/weight_far solved; `potential/weight_far[:,:,0]` ≈ `potential/weight_near[:,:,-1]` (continuity at interface)
- [ ] potential/weight_far[:,:,-1]` ≈ 0V everywhere (cathode)
close_reason: Code complete: bc-zstitch CLI fixed (--far-initial/--far-boundary); near-field weighting generator leaves z_min free for stitch. Execution sequence in Phase 6 shell script.

title: Phase 4 — Two-pass drift field FDM (far then near)
description:
## Why this issue exists

The drift field spans 150mm (z=0 to z=150mm). Near-field (z=0–10mm) uses dz=0.01mm to resolve the pixel-plane geometry accurately. Far-field (z=10–150mm) uses dz=0.5mm for efficiency. BCs originate at the cathode (far end), so far field is solved first; its z_min value (-500V) is then used as the z_max BC for the near-field solve.

## What needs to be done

Run two sequential FDM solves using the domains and generators from Phase 3 (far-field) and Phase 2 (near-field).

---

### Pass A — Far-field drift FDM (run first)

Prereqs: domain/drift_far and initial/drift_far, boundary/drift_far created by Phase 3 generator.

```bash
pochoir fdm     --initial initial/drift_far     --boundary boundary/drift_far     --potential potential/drift_far     --increment increment/drift_far     --edges per,per,fix     --engine torch     --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002
```

**Boundary conditions enforced:**
- z_min face (z=10mm): -500V fixed (set by generator)
- z_max face (z=150mm): -7500V fixed (set by generator)
- x, y faces: periodic

**Expected result:** potential/drift_far should be very close to the linear ramp (uniform 500V/cm field) since no lateral structure exists in the far field. FDM convergence should be fast.

---

### Pass B — Near-field drift FDM (run after Pass A)

Prereqs: domain/drift_near (44×44×1000, dz=0.01mm) and initial/drift_near, boundary/drift_near from Phase 2 generator (pixel plane drawn at z=0, z_max face fixed at -500V).

```bash
pochoir fdm     --initial initial/drift_near     --boundary boundary/drift_near     --potential potential/drift_near     --increment increment/drift_near     --edges per,per,fix     --engine torch     --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002
```

**Boundary conditions enforced:**
- z_min face (z=0): pixel plane at 0V, surrounding PCB/FR4 geometry drawn by Phase 2 generator
- z_max face (z=10mm): -500V fixed (set by Phase 2 generator)
- x, y faces: periodic

**Note:** Pass B does NOT depend on the output of Pass A — the z_max BC (-500V) for the near field is set analytically by the generator, not derived from the far-field FDM result. The two passes are independent in execution; the ordering constraint is conceptual only.

---

## Why -500V at z=10mm?

The far-field drift region spans 14cm (z=10mm to z=150mm). Assuming uniform drift field E=500V/cm:
- ΔV = 14cm × 500V/cm = 7000V
- Cathode at -7500V → potential at z=10mm = -7500 + 7000 = **-500V**

The near-field spans 1cm (z=0 to z=10mm) with the same 500V/cm → ΔV=500V, so 0V (pixel) to -500V (interface). Consistent.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] potential/drift_far solved; `potential/drift_far[:,:,0]` ≈ -500V everywhere (z=10mm face)
- [ ] potential/drift_far[:,:,-1]` ≈ -7500V everywhere (cathode face)
- [ ] Drift field E_z = -(potential/drift_far[:,:,1] - potential/drift_far[:,:,-1]) / (dz) ≈ -500V/cm in far field (uniform)
- [ ] potential/drift_near solved; `potential/drift_near[:,:,-1]` ≈ -500V everywhere (z=10mm face)
- [ ] potential/drift_near[:,:,0]` shows pixel structure (pixel pixels at 0V, surrounding area follows geometry BC)

title: Phase 3 — Far-field generators for drift and weighting
description:
## Why this issue exists

Phases 0–2 (anisotropic stencils, near-field domains, near-field generators) are complete. The far-field regions (z=10mm to z=150mm) need their own generator functions that set up initial and boundary arrays with no PCB/pixel geometry — only flat Dirichlet faces at z_min and z_max.

## What needs to be done

Create two new generator functions and register them in `pochoir/gen.py`.

---

### Generator 1: `pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far`

**File:** `pochoir/gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far.py` (new file, or add function to existing gen file and register)

**Domain:** 44 × 44 × 280, spacing (0.1, 0.1, 0.5) mm, origin (0, 0, 10) mm

**initial array (`initial/drift_far`):**
- Fill with a linear ramp in z:
  ```python
  for k in range(280):
      initial[:, :, k] = -500.0 + k * (-7500.0 - (-500.0)) / 279.0
  ```
  → k=0 gives -500V (z=10mm interface), k=279 gives -7500V (z=150mm cathode)
- All x,y columns identical (no lateral structure in far field)

**boundary array (`boundary/drift_far`):**
- All voxels: False (free) by default
- z_min face `[:, :, 0]` (z=10mm): set True — fixed BC at -500V
- z_max face `[:, :, -1]` (z=150mm): set True — fixed BC at CathodePotential (-7500V)
- x, y faces: NOT marked fixed (periodic BC handled by `--edges per,per,fix` at fdm time)
- Interior: False (free to evolve)

**Epsilon array:** uniform LAr permittivity (eps_r = 1.5) everywhere — no dielectric structure in far field.

**Config keys used:** `CathodePotential` (for z_max value). Interface value -500V is hardcoded (derived analytically: 14cm × 500V/cm = 7000V drop; -7500 + 7000 = -500V).

---

### Generator 2: `pcb_weight_pixel_with_grid_far`

**File:** `pochoir/gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid_far.py` (new file or add to existing)

**Domain:** 396 × 396 × 280, spacing (0.1, 0.1, 0.5) mm, origin (0, 0, 10) mm

**initial array (`initial/weight_far`):**
- Fill with zeros everywhere
- The z_min face will be overwritten by `pochoir bc-zstitch` after the near-field weighting FDM solve — do NOT set z_min values here

**boundary array (`boundary/weight_far`):**
- All voxels: False by default
- z_max face `[:, :, -1]` (z=150mm): set True — fixed BC at 0V (weighting field vanishes at cathode)
- z_min face `[:, :, 0]`: leave False — bc-zstitch will write the values AND set True after near-field solve
- x, y faces: NOT marked fixed (periodic)

**Epsilon array:** uniform LAr permittivity everywhere.

---

### Registration in gen.py

Add both new generators to the registry in `pochoir/gen.py` so they are discoverable by `pochoir gen --generator <name>`.

---

## Usage (how these will be called in Phase 6 script)

```bash
# Drift far-field
pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_far --shape=44,44,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far                --domain domain/drift_far                --initial initial/drift_far                --boundary boundary/drift_far                test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json

# Weighting far-field (run BEFORE bc-zstitch, AFTER domain creation)
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_far --shape=396,396,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_weight_pixel_with_grid_far                --domain domain/weight_far                --initial initial/weight_far                --boundary boundary/weight_far                test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far` generator creates initial/drift_far with linear ramp -500V→-7500V in z
- [ ] boundary/drift_far has z_min fixed at -500V and z_max fixed at -7500V; interior free
- [ ] `pcb_weight_pixel_with_grid_far` creates initial/weight_far all zeros; boundary z_max fixed at 0V; z_min free
- [ ] Both generators registered in gen.py and invocable via `pochoir gen --generator <name>`
- [ ] Epsilon arrays set to LAr eps_r=1.5 uniformly
close_reason: Implemented: gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far and gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid_far; both registered in gen.py; all acceptance criteria verified.

title: Near/far field separation with anisotropic z-spacing and 150mm drift
description:
## Why this issue exists

The current simulation uses a single uniform domain (0.1mm isotropic spacing) for the full 150mm drift length. This is inadequate: the weighting field varies rapidly near the pixel plane (z=0) and needs dz=0.01mm resolution there, but applying that resolution to the full 150mm drift would require 15000 z-slices — computationally prohibitive. Splitting into near (dz=0.01mm) and far (dz=0.5mm) regions solves both accuracy and cost.

## What needs to be done

### Phase 0 — Config and geometry baseline updates

Update JSON configs before anything else:
- `CathodePotential`: -7400 → **-7500 V**
- `pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition`: → **0** (pixel plane at z=0)
- `driftZDepth`: → **150.0 mm** (full cathode-to-pixel distance)

Files: `test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json`, `test/example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_eps.json`, small variant.

---

### Phase 1 — Anisotropic FDM stencils

**The problem:** `stencil()` in `pochoir/fdm_generic.py` computes the Laplace update with equal neighbor weights:
```
norm = 1/(2*nd)
φ_center = norm × Σ_all_neighbors
```
This is correct only for isotropic spacing. For spacing vector **(hx, hy, hz)** the correct Laplace update is:
```
φ_center = [Σ_d (φ_{d+} + φ_{d-}) / h_d²] / [Σ_d 2 / h_d²]
```
When hx=hy=0.1mm and hz=0.01mm, the z-neighbors carry 100× more weight than x/y neighbors.

**Changes:**
- `stencil(array, spacing=None, res=None)` — accept optional 1-D spacing array; use `1/h_d²` weights per dimension, normalize by `Σ 2/h_d²`; scalar/None falls back to current isotropic behavior
- `stencil_poisson(array, source=None, spacing=1.0, res=None)` — extend to accept vector spacing; source term denominator becomes `Σ 2/h_d²`
- `stencil_poisson_harmonic(phi, eps, spacing=None, res=None)` — same extension for harmonic-averaged epsilon; each dimension pair weighted by `1/h_d²`
- `fdm_torch.py solve()` — extract `domain.spacing` from params/context; pass as vector to stencil calls
- Backward compat: scalar spacing=1.0 or None produces identical output to current code

Files: `pochoir/fdm_generic.py`, `pochoir/fdm_torch.py`, `pochoir/fdm_numpy.py`

**Verification unit test:** isotropic hx=hy=hz=0.1 must give identical output to current stencil.

---

### Phase 2 — Near-field domains (drift and weighting)

**Drift near-field domain:**
- Shape: **(44, 44, 1000)**, spacing **(0.1, 0.1, 0.01) mm**, origin **(0, 0, 0) mm**
- Physical size: 4.4 mm × 4.4 mm × 10 mm

**Weighting near-field domain:**
- Shape: **(396, 396, 1000)**, spacing **(0.1, 0.1, 0.01) mm**, origin **(0, 0, 0) mm**
- Physical size: 39.6 mm × 39.6 mm × 10 mm

**Generator changes (`gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py`, `gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py`):**

All geometry indices currently computed as `int(physical_mm / dom.spacing[0])` — this works only when spacing is isotropic. With anisotropic spacing:
- x/y geometry (pixel size, gap, hole radius, chamfer): divide by `dom.spacing[0]` (0.1mm) — unchanged
- z geometry (pixel plane width, PCB thickness, driftZDepth boundary): divide by `dom.spacing[2]` (0.01mm in near field)

Generators draw geometry only up to z=10mm; the z_max face is left open (no cathode drawn here — it is the interface to the far field, whose BC is supplied analytically).

---

### Phase 3 — Far-field domains (drift and weighting)

**Drift far-field domain:**
- Shape: **(44, 44, 280)**, spacing **(0.1, 0.1, 0.5) mm**, origin **(0, 0, 10) mm**
- Physical size: 4.4 mm × 4.4 mm × 140 mm

**Weighting far-field domain:**
- Shape: **(396, 396, 280)**, spacing **(0.1, 0.1, 0.5) mm**, origin **(0, 0, 10) mm**
- Physical size: 39.6 mm × 39.6 mm × 140 mm

**Geometry:** No PCB or pixel structure exists beyond z=10mm. A new minimal generator (or flag in existing generator) sets:
- z_max face (z=150mm): uniform cathode BC for drift / uniform 0V for weighting
- z_min face (z=10mm): BC set analytically (drift) or from near-field result (weighting) — see Phases 4 and 5
- x,y faces: periodic

---

### Phase 4 — Two-pass drift field FDM

**Why -500V at z=1cm?** Far-field spans z=10mm→150mm (14cm). Uniform drift field: E=500 V/cm → ΔV=7000V over 14cm. Cathode at -7500V → potential at z=10mm = -7500+7000 = **-500V**. Near-field spans z=0→10mm (1cm) with the same 500V/cm → ΔV=500V, consistent (0V at pixel, -500V at z=10mm).

**Pass A — Far field first:**
```bash
pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_far --shape=44,44,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far --domain domain/drift_far ...
# generator sets: z_max face = -7500V, z_min face = -500V, x/y = periodic
pochoir fdm    --domain domain/drift_far --initial initial/drift_far --boundary boundary/drift_far                --potential potential/drift_far --edges per,per,fix ...
```

**Pass B — Near field:**
```bash
pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_near --shape=44,44,1000 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.01*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid --domain domain/drift_near ...
# generator draws pixel plane at z=0 (0V); z_max face = -500V
pochoir fdm    --domain domain/drift_near --initial initial/drift_near --boundary boundary/drift_near                --potential potential/drift_near --edges per,per,fix ...
```

---

### Phase 5 — Two-pass weighting field FDM

**Pass A — Near field first:**
```bash
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_near --shape=396,396,1000 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.01*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_pixel_with_grid --domain domain/weight_near ...
# generator: pixel of interest = +1V; all other pixel-plane pixels = 0V; z_max face open (0V BC initially)
pochoir fdm    --domain domain/weight_near ... --potential potential/weight_near --edges per,per,fix
```

After solve: extract the z_max boundary slice from `potential/weight_near` — a (396,396) array at z=10mm.

**Stitching (new CLI command `pochoir bc-zstitch`):**

`bc_interp.py` already handles 2D→3D stitching along the x-axis. A new analogous command stitches two 3D domains along z:
- Reads the z_max slice (`[:,:,-1]`) of the near-field potential
- Writes it as the z_min BC of the far-field initial/boundary arrays

Since x,y spacing is identical in both regions (0.1mm), direct index copy — no interpolation. Only z origin shifts from 0mm to 10mm.

**Pass B — Far field:**
```bash
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_far --shape=396,396,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'
pochoir bc-zstitch --near-potential potential/weight_near                    --far-initial initial/weight_far --far-boundary boundary/weight_far
# This sets z_min face of weight_far from near-field z=10mm slice
# z_max face (z=150mm) = 0V (weighting field vanishes at cathode)
pochoir fdm    --domain domain/weight_far ... --potential potential/weight_far --edges per,per,fix
```

---

### Phase 6 — Shell script / Makefile integration

Update the run script to execute in order:
1. Create near and far domains (drift, weighting)
2. Gen near-field geometry for drift and weighting
3. Gen far-field geometry (minimal: just cathode/open boundaries)
4. FDM drift far → FDM drift near
5. FDM weighting near → bc-zstitch → FDM weighting far
6. Velocity map from drift_near (unchanged downstream)
7. Drift electrons (unchanged)
8. Combine/extend weight fields (unchanged)

---

### Phase 7 — Verification and tests

Key assertions (`test/test_near_far_separation.py`):
- `potential/drift_near[:,:,-1]` ≈ **-500V** everywhere (z=10mm face)
- `potential/drift_far[:,:,0]` ≈ **-500V** everywhere (z=10mm face)
- `potential/drift_far[:,:,-1]` ≈ **-7500V** everywhere (cathode)
- Drift E_z ≈ **-500 V/cm** in far field (uniform)
- `potential/weight_near[:,:,-1]` ≈ `potential/weight_far[:,:,0]` (continuity at z=10mm)
- Weighting field ≈ **0V** at cathode

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Anisotropic stencil reproduces isotropic result when hx=hy=hz
- [ ] drift_near domain: 44×44×1000 at spacing (0.1,0.1,0.01)mm; drift_far: 44×44×280 at (0.1,0.1,0.5)mm
- [ ] weight_near domain: 396×396×1000 at spacing (0.1,0.1,0.01)mm; weight_far: 396×396×280 at (0.1,0.1,0.5)mm
- [ ] Drift field continuous and smooth at z=10mm; both sides read ≈-500V
- [ ] Weighting field near-field solved first; far-field BC at z=10mm from near-field result
- [ ] bc-zstitch command correctly copies z_max slice of near to z_min BC of far
- [ ] All assertions pass in test_near_far_separation.py
- [ ] End-to-end run script executes full workflow

## Design decisions

- **Two domains instead of non-uniform grid:** Extending the FDM engine to support rectilinear (variable-spacing) grids would require restructuring all stencils. Two separate uniform-spacing domains reuse existing infrastructure with only the anisotropic-spacing extension to stencils.
- **Far first for drift, near first for weighting:** Drift BCs originate at the cathode (far end) and propagate inward; the far-field z_min BC (-500V) can be set analytically. Weighting BCs originate at the pixel (z=0, near end) and propagate outward; the far-field z_min BC must come from the FDM result of the near-field solve.
- **bc-zstitch vs extending bc-interp:** `bc_interp.py` interpolates 2D→3D along the x-axis using SciPy RGI. Here x,y grids are identical in near and far (same 0.1mm pitch), so no interpolation is needed — just a direct slice copy. A separate command keeps the code clear and avoids overloading bc-interp.
- **-500V at z=1cm:** Chosen so the far-field drift matches a uniform 500V/cm field over the 14cm gap, consistent with the near-field drop of 500V over 1cm. This can be adjusted if the actual geometry shows significant deviation from uniformity near z=10mm.
notes:
## Missing detail: Far-field generator implementation (Phase 3 clarification)

Phase 3 was underspecified. Here is the concrete implementation plan a developer needs.

### Far-field generator: what it must produce

The far field (z=10mm to z=150mm) contains no PCB, no pixel structures — only two flat boundary faces at z_min and z_max. A new generator file `pochoir/gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far.py` (or a `--far` flag to the existing one) must build the initial and boundary arrays as follows.

#### Drift far-field arrays (44 × 44 × 280)

**initial array (`initial/drift_far`):**
- Fill with a linear ramp in z: value at voxel k = -500 + k × (-7500 - (-500)) / 279
  → z_min (k=0) = -500V, z_max (k=279) = -7500V
- This is not mandatory for correctness but dramatically accelerates FDM convergence because the true solution in the uniform region is close to a ramp.
- x, y: identical for all columns (uniform horizontal potential at each z-slice)

**boundary array (`boundary/drift_far`):**
- All voxels: False (free) by default
- z_min face `[:, :, 0]`: set True (fixed BC), values in initial = -500V everywhere
- z_max face `[:, :, -1]`: set True (fixed BC), values in initial = -7500V everywhere
- x, y faces: NOT marked fixed (will be handled by `--edges per,per,fix` periodic flag)
- Interior: False (free)

**pochoir gen invocation:**
```bash
pochoir gen --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far             --domain domain/drift_far             --initial initial/drift_far             --boundary boundary/drift_far             example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
```
The generator reads CathodePotential (-7500V) from the config for z_max and hardcodes -500V for z_min.

#### Weighting far-field arrays (396 × 396 × 280)

The weighting far-field generator cannot set the z_min face — that slice comes from bc-zstitch after the near-field FDM solve. So the generator only sets:

**initial array (`initial/weight_far`):**
- Fill with zeros (weighting field is ~0 in most of the far field; FDM will fill it in)

**boundary array (`boundary/weight_far`):**
- All voxels: False by default
- z_max face `[:, :, -1]`: True (fixed BC), values = 0V (weighting field vanishes at cathode)
- z_min face: leave all False initially — bc-zstitch will set the values AND mark those voxels as fixed BC after the near-field solve

**pochoir gen invocation:**
```bash
pochoir gen --generator pcb_weight_pixel_with_grid_far             --domain domain/weight_far             --initial initial/weight_far             --boundary boundary/weight_far             example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
```

### bc-zstitch: what it does in detail

Input:
- `--near-potential potential/weight_near`: the solved near-field potential array (396, 396, 1000)
- `--far-initial initial/weight_far`: the far-field initial array (396, 396, 280) to be updated
- `--far-boundary boundary/weight_far`: the far-field boundary array (396, 396, 280) to be updated

Operation:
1. Extract slice: `bc_slice = potential/weight_near[:, :, -1]` — shape (396, 396) at z=10mm
2. Write into far initial: `initial/weight_far[:, :, 0] = bc_slice`
3. Mark as fixed: `boundary/weight_far[:, :, 0] = True`
4. Save updated initial/weight_far and boundary/weight_far back to store

No interpolation needed: both domains have dx=dy=0.1mm so x,y indices are identical.

### Full command sequence for Phase 4 and 5

#### Drift field
```bash

pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_far  --shape=44,44,280  --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm'  --origin='0,0,10*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid_far --domain domain/drift_far                --initial initial/drift_far --boundary boundary/drift_far                example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
pochoir fdm    --initial initial/drift_far --boundary boundary/drift_far                --potential potential/drift_far --edges per,per,fix                --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002

# Near field (run after far)
pochoir domain --domain domain/drift_near --shape=44,44,1000 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.01*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid --domain domain/drift_near                --initial initial/drift_near --boundary boundary/drift_near                example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
pochoir fdm    --initial initial/drift_near --boundary boundary/drift_near                --potential potential/drift_near --edges per,per,fix                --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002
```

#### Weighting field
```bash
# Near field (run first)
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_near --shape=396,396,1000 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.01*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_pixel_with_grid --domain domain/weight_near                --initial initial/weight_near --boundary boundary/weight_near                example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
pochoir fdm    --initial initial/weight_near --boundary boundary/weight_near                --potential potential/weight_near --edges per,per,fix                --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002

# Stitch near->far
pochoir bc-zstitch --near-potential potential/weight_near                    --far-initial initial/weight_far --far-boundary boundary/weight_far

# Far field (run after stitch)
pochoir domain --domain domain/weight_far --shape=396,396,280 --spacing='0.1*mm,0.1*mm,0.5*mm' --origin='0,0,10*mm'
pochoir gen    --generator pcb_weight_pixel_with_grid_far --domain domain/weight_far                --initial initial/weight_far --boundary boundary/weight_far                example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.json
pochoir fdm    --initial initial/weight_far --boundary boundary/weight_far                --potential potential/weight_far --edges per,per,fix                --engine torch --nepochs 1 --epoch 20000 --precision 0.00002
```

Note: bc-zstitch must run AFTER weight_near FDM and BEFORE weight_far gen (or at minimum before weight_far FDM), since gen initializes the zero-value array and bc-zstitch overwrites the z_min face.

title: Fix FR4 slab placement in weighting-field gen (removes 2nd spike in (0,0) response)
description: The (0,0) field response has a spurious SECOND spike (a dip at z~3.7mm splitting it into two peaks); the physically-correct response is a single spike. Root cause: gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py places the FR4 PCB slab ABOVE the pad (z=[pp_loweredge+pp_width : +pcb_width] = 2.1-3.7mm, inside the LAr drift region), while gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py correctly places it BELOW the pad (epsilon[:,:,:pp_loweredge]=FR4). The electron drifting through the LAr crosses the spurious FR4/LAr interface at z=3.7mm in the weighting field, where grad(W) jumps by ~eps ratio (4.4/1.505) -> dQ/dt dip -> second spike. Verified: deep correctedSym run was clean only because it used NO epsilon (uniform); drift path is uniform (drift field has no slab there) -> the two generators are geometrically inconsistent.
design: Fix gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py to place FR4 BELOW the pad, mirroring the drift gen (and its aperture/hole LAr-mask handling). New z-range: z_pcb=[max(0,pp_loweredge-pcb_width) : pp_loweredge]. Update the per-pixel tiling block (lines ~248-274) and the aperture (LAr-filled hole) mask to the new z-range. Keep the pad/PixelPermittivity assignment at z=pp_loweredge. VERIFY: (a) epsilon center column = LAr for z>pad, FR4 below pad, pad-metal at z=2; (b) W(z) along pad-center has smooth monotonic gradient (no kink at z~3.7); (c) re-run drift+induce (edge-start, depth-400 weight) -> compare_fr_tred shows SINGLE spike at (0,0), cosine improves toward deep-quality (>0.97), integral ~0.994. Add a regression assert that weight-gen and drift-gen FR4 z-placement agree.
acceptance_criteria: (0,0) waveform is single-peaked (no pre-peak dip); center-pixel cosine vs tred > 0.97; epsilon places FR4 below pad consistent with drift gen.

(0,0) response is now a single spike (was two); center cosine 0.957->0.991, center peak 0.588->0.731 (~tred 0.73), integral 0.995. W(z) gradient smooth at z=3.7mm (interface kink gone). Committed.
